what: A `configure` hook attempted async work (returned a Promise).
fix: Make `configure` synchronous and move async work to `boot`.

what: A `configure` hook threw.
fix: Fix the unit's config or its `configure` hook, then build a new app.

what: A `boot` hook threw.
fix: Read `cause` and `plugin`, then fix that unit's `boot` hook or the service it opens.

what: A `start` hook threw.
fix: Read `cause` and `plugin`, then fix that unit's `start` hook.

what: One or more `stop` hooks threw — aggregate.
fix: Read `failures`: each entry names the unit whose `stop` hook threw.

what: One or more `dispose` hooks threw — aggregate.
fix: Read `failures`: each entry names the unit whose `dispose` hook threw.

what: Caller tried to reuse the app after dispose.
fix: Build a fresh app instance; a disposed app cannot run again.

what: Caller tried to reuse the app after a failed lifecycle.
fix: Build a fresh app instance; a failed app cannot run again.

what: Unit registered twice.
fix: Remove the second `.infra()` of this unit, or `rename` it to run two copies.

what: A unit's `needs` entry has no provider among earlier-booted units.
fix: Mount a unit that provides the needed key before its consumer.

what: A unit published a wire key that an earlier unit already provides.
fix: Give one of the two providers a different key with `rename`.

what: A needs alias, publish key, or rename target uses the reserved `$` prefix.
fix: Rename the key; names starting with `$` belong to the kernel.

what: A lifecycle hook exceeded the app's `hookTimeoutMs` watchdog.
fix: Pass the hook's `$signal` to its I/O, or raise `hookTimeoutMs` with a reason.

what: Two actions in the same binding use the same id.
fix: Give each action in a binding its own id.

what: Action metadata is not JSON-round-trip safe.
fix: Keep action `meta` plain JSON: no functions, Dates, Maps or cycles.

what: More than one unit fills the logging slot.
fix: Keep one `log()` unit in the app.

what: Static capability needs form a ring: a feature's need comes back around to itself.
fix: Move the shared piece into a third unit that both sides need.

what: A feature needs a capability whose (static) provider is mounted after it.
fix: Mount the provider before the unit that needs it; the message names both positions.

what: `$describeAction` named an action the calling unit may not amend (unknown id, or not its own).
fix: Describe only actions the calling unit declared or owns.

what: Two routers of a feature use the same key.
fix: Rename one of the two router keys.

what: Two repos of a feature use the same key.
fix: Rename one of the two repo keys.

what: Two slices of a feature use the same key.
fix: Rename one of the two slice keys.

what: A feature was declared with no slices.
fix: Add at least one slice to the feature.

what: A handle the feature needs is missing from the services bag.
fix: Mount the provider of that handle, and check the gateway's needs.

what: A need alias, infra key, provided key or entrypoint key collides with another slot or a reserved name.
fix: Rename the alias or key so it collides with nothing.

what: `override()` named a key that no infra unit of the feature provides.
fix: Override a key that one of the feature's infra units provides.

what: `routerFor()`: an app-contract key is implemented by zero or several features.
fix: Give each app-contract key exactly one feature.

what: `routerFor()`: a feature's contract is not mounted in the app contract.
fix: Mount the feature's contract in the app contract.

what: `rpc()`: a procedure's contract `meta` is not plain JSON, so `dot explain` cannot show it.
fix: Keep the procedure's contract `meta` plain JSON.

what: A unit was mounted on the wrong side of the hexagon: an `entrypoint` in `.infra()` / `.infra()`, or an `infra` or `feature` unit in `.entrypoints()` / `.entrypoints()`. Typed graphs refuse this at compile time; this catches erased ones.
fix: Mount infra with `.infra(...)` and entrypoints with `.entrypoints(...)`, or build the unit with the other constructor.

what: A feature needs `domainService(fn)` that no parent declares above `.features()`: the parent never passed `fn` to `.domainServices()`, or the feature is top-level.
fix: Pass the factory to the parent's `.domainServices({ … })` before `.features()`, and need it only from that parent's children.

what: `.domainServices()` ran twice, or after `.features()`, `.usecases()` or `.provides()`.
fix: Declare every domain service in one `.domainServices({ … })` call, right after `.infra()`.

what: The env failed its schema at boot. The message lists every bad key.
fix: Set the listed variables, or fix their values, before booting the app.

what: `boot` ran before the kernel activated the logging slot.
fix: Mount `log()` with `.infra()` in a Dot app and let the kernel run its hooks; never call them yourself.

what: Approval must be verified for this invocation, not inferred from another exposure.
fix: Verify approval bound to the caller, action and input.

what: An adapter may call only an explicitly exposed boundary.
fix: Use an adapter listed by the action contract.

what: The adapter must authenticate its caller before invoking this action.
fix: Authenticate the caller before invoking the action.

what: Importing the app file threw, or its exported factory did.
fix: Apply `.error.data.causeRemediation` when it is set; otherwise run `bun <app file>` to reproduce.

what: The app file loaded, but no export is a DOT app, or several are and none is `default` or `app`.
fix: Export the app as `default` or as `app`.

what: `configure` threw while the CLI prepared the app.
fix: Read `.error.data.underlyingCode` and look it up in the kernel error table; `ARKI_DOT_E020` means a provider is mounted after its consumer.

what: No app file at the default paths and no `--app`.
fix: Create `dot.config.ts` that exports the app, or pass `--app <path>`.

what: Another `dot dev` is alive in this project: its pid is in the state file.
fix: Stop the other `dot dev`; if its pid is not a `dot dev`, delete the file in `.error.data.statePath`.

what: The app export is already configured, booted or started: `dot dev` cannot own its lifecycle.
fix: Export the unstarted builder: no `configure()`, `boot()` or `start()` call on the `dev` export.

what: `dot dev` found no Postgres to talk to: no URL, a bad URL, or a closed port it could not start.
fix: Start the database, fix `DB_URL` in `.env`, or run `dot dev --db pglite`.

what: Something already listens on the app port, so the runner would not get it.
fix: Stop the process on that port, or pick another one with `dot dev --port <n>`.

what: The preflight process did not report a result: a crash, a hang past the timeout, or output that is not its report. Never a pass.
fix: Read `.error.data.output`, then run `dot doctor --app <file>` to see the same boot in the foreground.

what: The database is neither on this machine nor a compose service: `dot dev` would migrate it on boot.
fix: Point every database URL at this machine or a compose service, or pass `--allow-remote-db` on purpose.

what: The app runner (`vite dev`, `--run`, or `dot _serve`) could not be started.
fix: Install the runner, or pass the command that serves the app with `dot dev --run "<cmd>"`.

what: `doctor` found error-severity issues. The data is the whole report: `.error.data.plugins[]`.
fix: Apply the `remediation` of each issue in `.error.data.plugins[].issues` and `.error.data.issues`.

what: `dot env check` found at least one error.
fix: Work through `.error.data.findings`; each has its own `remediation`.

what: The command after `--` could not be started.
fix: Check the command name and PATH.

what: Decrypting a tracked file would put plaintext secrets one `git add` away from a commit.
fix: Pass `--force` if you really mean it, and do not commit the result.

what: The key is in none of the loaded env files.
fix: Check the name and `--env`; `dot env ls` lists the keys.

what: The env files could not be loaded: a private key is missing, a value cannot be decrypted, or a reference cannot be resolved.
fix: Follow the message of each entry in `.error.data.errors` (codes `ARKI_ENV_FILES_E00x`).

what: The command would write nothing: the value is already there, or there was nothing to encrypt or decrypt.
fix: Read `.error.data.reason`; a variable exported in the shell does not change the file.

what: The file has no dotenvx public key header, so values cannot be encrypted into it.
fix: Run `dot env init` with the same `--env`/`--file`.

what: `--plain` was asked for a key the env schema declares with `secret()`.
fix: Drop `--plain`: a secret must be encrypted in a tracked file.

what: A value was asked for where it would leave the terminal (a pipe, a file, an agent's transcript).
fix: Run `dot env get <KEY> --reveal` in an interactive terminal, or `dot env run -- <cmd>` to hand values to a process.

what: The value came from both a positional argument and `--stdin`, or from neither.
fix: Give exactly one: `dot env set KEY value`, or `printf %s "$VALUE" | dot env set KEY --stdin`.

what: The 1Password CLI (`op`) failed or is not signed in.
fix: Install `op`, sign in (`op signin`), and check the vault name.

what: A vault write was attempted but its result was not confirmed.
fix: Read the item from 1Password before retrying; the write may already have completed.

what: An operation tried to initialize a service after its owner closed admission.
fix: Use the handle only while its owning application is running.

what: `doctor --observability` found no OpenTelemetry SDK. Reported as a warning issue in the snapshot, not returned.
fix: Register an OpenTelemetry SDK once at app entry, before any app boots.

what: A managed preflight reported a lifecycle failure, retaining the complete report.
fix: Read `.error.data.failure.code` and apply its message; inspect `.error.data.report` for diagnostics.

what: Two units register different modules for one projection format.
fix: Remove one registration, or make both units register the same module.

what: `project(manifest)` threw or returned output that does not survive a JSON round trip.
fix: Make `project(manifest)` pure and return JSON-round-trip-safe output.

what: The projection module could not be resolved or imported, or exports no `project(manifest)`.
fix: Install the module and export a named `project(manifest)` function from it.

what: No unit registers the `--as` format.
fix: Use a format from `.error.data.registeredFormats`, or mount the adapter that provides it.

what: Previous ownership could not be released, so starting another app is unsafe.
fix: Resolve the disposal failure before starting another owner of the resources.

what: A replaced module no longer owns the application's runtime.
fix: Obtain the runtime exported by the current module.

what: `dot new` would overwrite files in a non-empty target directory.
fix: Choose an empty directory, or re-run with `--force` to overwrite.

what: The package's bundled template directory is empty or missing.
fix: Reinstall `@arki/dot`: it must ship its `templates/` directory.

what: `dot new` could not write some files. `written` lists the ones that landed.
fix: Check the permissions of the target directory, then re-run with `--force`.
